title: Synapse Analytics: dedicated and serverless SQL pools

videos.script: Every night Quitanda wants the same report: sales per store per day, over the whole year. {{report}} A database built to fetch one order by its id is slow at that. A warehouse is built for it. {{warehouse}} Synapse Analytics offers two. A dedicated SQL pool is a warehouse you provision and pay for by the hour. It spreads every table over sixty distributions. {{dedicated}} Where each row goes is a decision in the table's definition. Get it wrong and one distribution does the work while the others wait. {{skew}} A serverless SQL pool provisions nothing. It reads files in the lake where they lie, and charges for the bytes it processes. {{serverless}} No emulator runs Synapse. So this lesson puts a month of Quitanda's orders into Azurite, as CSV and as Parquet. {{lake}} Then DuckDB, a small engine inside a Python program, asks the same question of both, and counts every byte it pulls out. DuckDB is the stand-in, and the lesson says so every time. {{duckdb}} The same answer reads thirty-five megabytes, or a quarter of one. The difference is the file format and the folders. {{bytes}}
